title: Landing guards assume a rule id is one directory name, so packaged and nested rules escape the conflict guard and the evidence pin
where: Horde skills/horde/scripts/land.mjs:1448 (ASPECT_TEXT_FILE), :2651 (lawTrailers), :1702 (evidencePinAt), :1833 (comment 'A rule id is a bare directory name')
evidence: land.mjs:1448 `/^\.yggdrasil\/aspects\/([^/]+)\/(content\.md|check\.mjs|companion\.mjs|yg-aspect\.yaml)$/`. Tested with node: `.yggdrasil/aspects/boundary/clean-core/content.md` → false; `.yggdrasil/aspects/packages/promises/has-evidence/check.mjs` → false; `.yggdrasil/aspects/prose/helpers/x.mjs` → false. Yggdrasil docs/packages.md:28-30 and :51-53: `yg pack add` copies into `.yggdrasil/aspects/packages/<owner>/<repo>/<pkg>/`, the rule id is `packages/acme/law/house-style/naming`, and adaptations (status, review_by, scope, config) live in `yg-aspect.adapt.yaml` beside the rule (packages.md:130-160). horde.mjs:322 itself tells adopters to run `yg pack add …#promises`. Yet evidencePinAt reads `.yggdrasil/aspects/has-evidence/yg-aspect.yaml` (land.mjs:1702), a path that install never creates, so a pinned `evidence: mirror` in the adapt file is ignored and the gate falls back to `auto`. audit.mjs:568-571 already knows ids contain `/` (`boundary/clean-core`); horde.mjs:248 matches `/(^|\/)doc-shape$/`. Only land.mjs kept the single-segment assumption. A branch that rewrites a packaged or nested rule's content.md together with code that rule reaches lands with no conflict-of-interest refusal. Its merge trailer reads `Law: packages changed` or `Law: boundary changed`.
proposal: Resolve every changed path under `.yggdrasil/aspects/` to a rule id by longest-prefix match against the ids in the base and head `yg aspects --json` documents, which Horde already reads in lawGuard. Do not use a regex. Treat any file inside the rule's directory, plus `yg-aspect.adapt.yaml`, as the rule's text; 6.1.0 hashes a prose rule's whole directory. Read the has-evidence pin by finding the rule whose id ends in `has-evidence`, then its adapt file (installed) or its yg-aspect.yaml (hand-copied). Better long term: ask Yggdrasil to add a per-rule `definitionHash` to yg-aspects/1 (a hash of the rule's verdict inputs). The conflict and law guards would then compare two hashes instead of listing files. Cost: about 60 lines in land.mjs plus 3 fixtures (nested id, installed package, adapt-file pin). The Yggdrasil field is a separate small additive change. Success: a fixture branch that edits `.yggdrasil/aspects/packages/o/r/promises/has-evidence/content.md` together with a promise it reaches is refused as a conflict of interest, and a pin written in the adapt file changes the pairing the gate uses.
effort: S-M (1 day Horde; optional 0.5 day Yggdrasil for definitionHash)

title: The landing's free half is still read as text, costs two graph runs, and misdiagnoses a log-gate abort as a missing reviewer
evidence: fillDeterministic runs `check --approve --only-deterministic` without `--json` and returns `out: run.out + run.err` (node.mjs:531). checkGraph then runs a second full `check --no-approve --json` (land.mjs:1002). When script pairs remain, it dumps the fill's raw text with the diagnosis 'the free half did not take — … most often because a judgement rule has no judge configured' (land.mjs:1008). On 6.1.0 that diagnosis is wrong. In scratch repo $TMPDIR/hordeyg-b, with no reviewer configured, the free fill still filled the script pair (`[["nomark","approved"],["prose","unverified"]]`). The only thing that stops the free half is a gate. In $TMPDIR/hordeyg-a, with `log_required: true`, `yg check --approve --only-deterministic --json` returned `exit.status: "aborted"`, `aborted: {stage: "log-gate", issues: [{code: "log-entry-missing", node: "pay"…}]}` and `next.target: {node: "pay"}`. In $TMPDIR/hordeyg-c the same command with `--json --compact` printed the post-fill yg-check/1 document (`nomark approved`, 1 pair listed), so the fill and the read can be one run.
proposal: Replace fillDeterministic plus runYgCheck in checkGraph with one call: `yg check --approve --only-deterministic --json --compact`. Branch on its fields. `exit.status === 'aborted'` goes to the aborted stage: for `log-gate`, name `aborted.issues[].node` and the `yg log add` step from `next`; for `structural`, name the issues. Otherwise read the pending prose pairs from `pairs` exactly as now. The compact form keeps only non-approved pairs, which is all the landing needs. Delete the stale comment. Cost: about 80 lines changed in node.mjs and land.mjs, plus 2 fixtures (a log-gate abort and a structural abort). Success: a landing on a log_required node with no entry returns one graph item that names the node and the `yg log add` step, never 'no judge configured'. The landing's graph item runs one `yg check` process where it now runs two; count spawns in a test with a wrapped ygCommand.

title: Refusals no worker can fix tick fix rounds; 6.1.0's cause/remaining say which they are
where: Horde land.mjs:1037-1054 (checkJudge), land.mjs:3679-3690 (recordChanges), land.mjs:3569-3571 (the only no-round exception), node.mjs:497-511 (hasReviewer), horde.mjs:562-575 (init)
evidence: recordChanges ticks the round counter for every red item (land.mjs:3679-3690). The only exemption is a stale base (land.mjs:3569: 'Not a red gate and not a fix round — the ticket did nothing wrong'). A tree whose prose pairs have no reviewer is refused in checkJudge with 'configure one (yg init --provider …)'. That decision belongs to the user, and yg says so: in the scratch run, `next.requiresUser: true`, `next.remaining: {needsFix:0, fillable:1, needsUser:1, waitingOnReviewer:1}`, issue `cause: "reviewer-missing"`, code `config-reviewer-missing`, why 'Configuring a reviewer is the user's decision'. Every ticket touching such a node bounces until it reaches `stuck`. horde init refuses only when a commit hook runs a full check (horde.mjs:567). With no hook it starts the mission anyway. The answer 'is there a reviewer' comes from a YAML regex over yg-config.yaml and yg-secrets.yaml (node.mjs:497-511), not from the graph. The 6.1.0 ruling that Yggdrasil's reviewer is the one judge (that loop's decisions.md:105-106) says Horde refuses such landings, not that it should spend rounds on them.
proposal: Classify each red graph item by the document's own buckets. If `next.remaining.needsFix === 0 && fillable === 0` and `needsUser + waitingOnReviewer > 0`, or every blocking unverified issue has `cause` in {reviewer-missing, reviewer-unreachable, reviewer-failed}, the refusal is not the ticket's. Record it like the stale-base path: no round, and raise one director-level item per horde (an `ask` or a status line) carrying `next.text`, not one per ticket. At `horde init` and in `refine --step frame`, run a read-only `check --json` and put any `config-reviewer-missing` or `waitingOnReviewer > 0` before the user during framing, the only phase with the user in the loop. Delete hasReviewer in favour of the `reviewer-missing` cause. Cost: about 100 lines in land.mjs, horde.mjs and node.mjs; 3 fixtures. Success: in a fixture with an enforced prose rule and no reviewer, two tickets on that node both show 'waiting on a user decision', neither ticks a round, one ask exists, and the charter frame names the gap.

v.reason: Confirmed. recordChanges (land.mjs:3683-3693) ticks a round on any red item, and only the stale path (:3569-3575) is exempt. checkJudge (:1037-1054) refuses with 'configure one', using the YAML-regex hasReviewer (node.mjs:497-511). horde.mjs:566-575 refuses init only when a hook runs a full check. My scratch re-run gave `next.requiresUser: true` and `remaining {needsFix:0, fillable:0, needsUser:1, waitingOnReviewer:1}`, with issue cause `reviewer-missing` and code `config-reviewer-missing`. So every ticket on such a node burns rounds until it is stuck, for a decision that the 6.1.0 ruling on Yggdrasil's reviewer as the one judge leaves with the user. Not filed in the loop.

title: Under Horde the yg log gate goes quiet after the first entry: landings only run the free fill, and log-cycle-open is never read
where: Horde reference/roles/worker.md:86-91; land.mjs:990 (fill); Yggdrasil docs/cli-reference.md:813,851, docs/the-lock.md:87
evidence: Yggdrasil docs/the-lock.md:87: '--only-deterministic … never ends a node's log cycle … the newest entry a node has goes on satisfying the requirement for every later source change … Plain `yg check` says when this has happened: … a `log-cycle-open` warning.' The worker brief frames the full fill as the prose-rule step: 'What is left after that free run is the prose rules … `yg check --approve` calls it' (worker.md:88-90). The landing runs only `--only-deterministic`. Horde never reads `log-cycle-open`: grep over scripts/ finds 0 hits. Reproduced in $TMPDIR/hordeyg-a with a script-only log_required node `ship`: one `yg log add`, then two commits each followed by `--only-deterministic` (both exit 0). Plain `check --json` returned `exit.status: pass`, with `["log-cycle-open","warning","ship"]`. The second edit was never asked for its why.
proposal: Two cheap parts. (a) Worker brief: before the final commit, run `yg check --approve --dry-run --json`. If `next.cost.reviewerPairs` (or `dryRunBudget`) is 0, run the full `yg check --approve` anyway. It is free, closes the cycle, and records the baseline in the committed lock; commit it. (b) Landing: a `log-cycle-open` issue on a node the branch changed turns the graph item red, with the node and 'record why, run the free full fill, commit the lock'. Cost: about 30 lines plus the brief text; 1 fixture reusing the scratch sequence above. Success: the scratch sequence run through land.mjs refuses the second ticket until a new entry exists. A mission's trunk shows 0 `log-cycle-open` warnings at wave close.

v.reason: Confirmed. Yggdrasil docs/the-lock.md:87 says the free gate never ends a node's log cycle, and that plain check warns `log-cycle-open`. `/usr/bin/grep` over Horde scripts finds no read of log-cycle-open. worker.md:86-91 makes the full `--approve` read as a prose-rule step only, so on a script-only node the free fill is all that runs. Real but narrow: it matters only for log_required nodes with no prose rules. Part (a) of the proposal is cheap.

title: The wave quality index counts cache state and Horde's own process as 'the graph got weaker'
where: Horde node.mjs:639-695 (ygQualityIndex: baseline, noiseFloor, advisoryClean), wave.mjs:857-883 (measureQuality, qualityDecline)
evidence: `baseline: check.totals.errors` and `noiseFloor: check.totals.warnings` (node.mjs:678-679). `advisoryClean` treats any non-approved pair as 'something against it' (node.mjs:660-662). measureQuality reads the trunk with no free fill first (wave.mjs:857-864; no fillDeterministic in wave.mjs). The landing fills in a throwaway worktree, and the cache is gitignored, so the trunk's script pairs go stale after every merge. Reproduced in $TMPDIR/hordeyg-c: after one commit on a filled tree, `totals.errors: 3` included `["nomark","stale","error"]`, a script pair that is free to clear. After a Yggdrasil upgrade, the `keyed-by-earlier-release` cause re-opens every script pair once. `log-cycle-open` warnings (F4) land in noiseFloor. qualityDecline reports any rise as a fall ('blocking violations X → Y', 'noise floor X → Y'), and SKILL.md:258-262 says a fall is named to the chairman.
proposal: In ygQualityIndex, exclude from baseline and advisoryClean every pair with `kind === 'deterministic'` and verdict `unverified` or `stale`, plus every issue whose `cause` is `deterministic-not-run` or `keyed-by-earlier-release`. These are 'free to run', not violations. Report them as a separate `unfilled` figure. Exclude `log-cycle-open` from noiseFloor, or report it under its own name. Alternative: run the free fill on the trunk tree before measuring. It writes only the gitignored cache, which the architect brief already permits. Cost: about 25 lines; 1 fixture that merges a change and closes a wave without filling. Success: in that fixture, two consecutive wave closes with no rule or code-quality change report Δ baseline 0 and Δ noise floor 0.

v.reason: Confirmed in code. node.mjs:675-679 uses `baseline: totals.errors` and `noiseFloor: totals.warnings`. advisoryClean (:660-662) counts any non-approved pair against a rule. wave.mjs:857-864 measureQuality never fills first. The scratch config gitignores `.yg-lock.deterministic.json`, so script pairs on the trunk tree go unverified or stale after merges and read as 'blocking violations X → Y' (qualityDecline :868-883). The proposal is sound. The alternative (run the free fill on the trunk before measuring) is the simpler fix.

title: The advise sweep ignores evidenceHash and item class: a re-raised item is dropped, and lowerings and promotions become worker tickets
evidence: The ledger key is `advise:${item.id}` (audit.mjs:505), and an existing key is skipped as 'already filed as a ticket' (audit.mjs:521-524). yg-advise/1 items carry `evidenceHash` (scratch: `promotion:nomark` → `evidenceHash: 38356cc5…`). Yggdrasil binds decisions to it: an item 'returns to the feed as new' when its evidence changes (Yggdrasil CHANGELOG, advise dismiss/defer entry). Horde keys on the id alone, so the same id with new evidence is never refiled in that horde. Only `overdue-review-by:` and `imported:` are routed specially (audit.mjs:508-518). Every other class becomes a generic `quality` ticket for a worker. That includes `promotion:` (Horde's own ladder, node.mjs promote, rules that raising is the horde's own call, while yg's `next` says 'ask the user to approve it first'), `decorative-rule:` (a demotion, which the law guard refuses from any worker), and `sharpen:`/`drill-miss:` (the legislator's work). The class list comes from Yggdrasil source/cli/src/core/advise*.ts: architecture-cut, dead-attach, decorative-rule, drill-miss, family-without-law, imported, orphaned-aspect, overdue-review-by, package-update, promotion, sharpen, suppress-anomaly, type-covered-churn, uncovered-hot-spot.
proposal: Key the ledger by `${item.id}@${item.evidenceHash}` so a changed item is filed again and an unchanged one never is. Add a class routing table in audit.mjs: `promotion:` → feed the rule into the ladder's own evidence check and report, never a ticket. `decorative-rule:`, `dead-attach:`, `orphaned-aspect:`, `suppress-anomaly:`, `package-update:` → an ask of kind `lower` or `charter` for the client. `uncovered-hot-spot:`, `family-without-law:`, `type-covered-churn:`, `sharpen:`, `drill-miss:` → the territory's legislate pass. `architecture-cut:` → the architect. Cost: about 60 lines plus a table test per class. Success: in a fixture with a promotion item and a decorative-rule item, neither becomes a worker ticket. Re-running the close after the item's evidence changes files one new item.

v.reason: Confirmed. audit.mjs:505 keys the ledger by `advise:${item.id}` only, and :520-523 skips an item already on file. Only `overdue-review-by:` and `imported:` are routed (:508-518). adviseTicketBody (:355-387) sends every other class to a worker as a generic ticket. Yggdrasil core/advise-nominations.ts:94, :524 carries `evidenceHash` per item. Issue 118 fixed only the drill-miss id split, not routing or the hash. One caveat for the implementer: some evidence snapshots can change every wave, so keying on the hash can churn. Refile only when the item is not already open.

title: Relation findings carry edges now, and type-only imports are edges; the landing neither routes them nor separates inherited findings from new ones
where: Horde land.mjs:1016-1021 (checkGraph's generic refusal), node.mjs:564-570 (checkSummary: first blocking finding only); Yggdrasil CHANGELOG 6.1.0 Breaking (relation check), the 6.1.0 ruling that a type import is a dependency (decisions.md:111-112)
evidence: 6.1.0: 'a repository that passed can now report `relation-undeclared-dependency` for dependencies that were always in the code', and every type-only import is now a blocking edge (decisions.md:112; 191 relations added to Yggdrasil's own graph, CHANGELOG repo-internal note). yg-check/1 relation findings carry `edges: [{file, line, target}]` and `groups` (cli-reference.md, the check JSON section). Horde's graph item on any other red is one line: 'the graph refuses this tree' plus the first blocking `what` (land.mjs:1016-1021, node.mjs:567-569). Declaring a relation means editing yg-node.yaml, which is the architect's to approve (architect.md:33-39). A worker whose ticket adds a cross-node import cannot fix it and burns rounds. The landing never compares against the parent (the `progressive` field is read only into the quality index, node.mjs:694). A trunk that turned red on a Yggdrasil upgrade therefore refuses every landing.
proposal: In checkGraph, key blocking issues by `code + unitRef` and also read the parent tree's document, which the gate already has a base worktree for. Label each finding `introduced` or `already on <parent>`. Only introduced ones are the ticket's round; inherited ones go to one director item. For `relation-undeclared-dependency` whose `edges[].file` are in the branch's diff, put the edges and the relation stanza from the finding's `next` into a graph proposal for the architect (`node.mjs` proposal path), not a worker round. Render every `groups[]` entry (label, subject, member count, next) in the changes note, not just the first `what`, so one round shows everything to fix. Cost: 1-2 days; the second check on the base doubles graph time only on red landings. Success: a fixture that adds `import type` across two nodes produces an architect proposal naming file:line, and a fixture with a pre-red trunk lands a clean ticket with an 'inherited' note.

v.reason: Confirmed. node.mjs:565-571 checkSummary shows only the first blocking `what`. land.mjs:1016-1021 gives a generic 'the graph refuses this tree' with no comparison to the parent. The 6.1.0 ruling that a type import is a dependency (decisions.md:111-112) makes type-only imports blocking edges, so trunks that were green can turn red on upgrade. Splitting inherited from introduced findings is the valuable core. The architect-routing part should first check whether a worker may already add a relation within scope: worker.md does not forbid editing yg-node.yaml, and architect.md:33-39 covers approved graph changes.

title: Retire the 6.0.x text fallbacks at the next family release: parse codes, not English
where: Horde node.mjs:189 (YG_DOCUMENTS_AFTER='6.0.0'), node.mjs:333-345 and :383-384 (regex over stderr and what), node.mjs:731-767 (parseDrillSummary), node.mjs:866-872 (drill retry without --json), audit.mjs:159-260 (parseHealth, runHealth, NO_HEALTH_DOCUMENT), node.mjs:682-688 (coverage split fallback)
evidence: Horde keeps a second, text-reading path for every 6.1.0 document because 'the version floor still allows' 6.0.x (node.mjs:731, audit.mjs:167). ygErrorState still decides 'stale' by `/unknown option|unknown command/i` over text (node.mjs:338, :384), though 6.1.0 answers `code: "usage"`. Scratch run: `yg drill --bogus --json` → `{"schema":"yg-error/1","code":"usage",…,"next":{"command":["yg","drill","--help"],…}}`. Only `next.text` is ever read; `next.command` is dropped (node.mjs:341, :857). The release-readiness report kept the floor at 6.0.0 on purpose for 6.1 (2026-09-24 report, line 211). Under the one-number policy (Horde CHANGELOG:5) the next core release ships Horde and Yggdrasil together, so the fallback serves only a mixed install the policy already tells adopters to avoid.
proposal: In the next family release, raise YG_DOCUMENTS_AFTER (and LAW_CLI_AFTER, law.mjs:68) to 6.1.0. Delete parseDrillSummary, parseHealth, runHealth, NODE_MISSING_TEXT, the drill retry, both `unknown option` regexes and the coverage-split fallback. Treat yg-error/1 `code === 'usage'` as the stale signal, and carry `next.command` (argv) where a refusal prints a step. Cost: a net deletion of roughly 150-200 lines and their 6.0-only tests; the CHANGELOG states the new floor. Success: grep in scripts/ finds no regex over Yggdrasil prose (only schema and code checks), and the suite passes against 6.1.0 alone.

title: tick reclaims live workers: it commits their WIP, hands the ticket out twice, and reviews half-done branches
where: Horde skills/horde/scripts/queue.mjs:1717-1775 (reconcileRunningLocked), tick.mjs:831 (called unconditionally in runOnce), tick.mjs:776-800 (externalStart: detached, stdio ignore, no pid kept), SKILL.md:243 (20–30 min wake-ups), horde.mjs:402 (tick.interval 300)
evidence: reconcileRunning treats every `running` item as a call that has already returned. With commits beyond the parent it sets `item.state = 'landed'` (queue.mjs:1733). With a dirty tree it runs `git add -A && git commit -m 'wip: reclaimed'` inside the worker's worktree and re-queues the item (queue.mjs:1745). With a clean tree it removes the worktree (queue.mjs:1759). Nothing records whether a worker is still alive, although gates already get pid tracking (tick.mjs:357 processAlive). Scratch experiment live-worker.mjs: a ticket set running, one file written into its worktree, then a bare `tick.mjs` printed `reconciled [{"ticket":"001","state":"queued","note":"worktree was dirty — committed as \"wip: reclaimed\"…"}]` and `spawn [{"ticket":"001",…same worktree}]`, which is a second worker into the same tree. live-worker-bc.mjs: a worker that had made one stage commit ('red test first') was marked `landed` and got `review raised on c18c1dd…` at once, while a just-started worker's item went back to `queued`. The tick.mjs header says the caller "runs tick again once they come back", but SKILL.md:243 says to call tick every 20–30 minutes from a wake-up, and `--runner external --watch` spawns detached workers and re-ticks every 300 s. Under the foreground session runner the opposite cost applies: every batch waits for its slowest worker before anything lands.
proposal: Give a running item a lease that reconcile respects. (1) At dispatch, write `item.worker = {name, startedAt, pid?}`, and under the external runner record `child.pid` (externalStart already has it). (2) Reconcile settles an item only when there is evidence the worker ended: its mandated last line `tk.mjs log NNN "landed <sha>"` exists, or its pid is gone (external), or the director says so explicitly with `queue.mjs set NNN returned` / `tick --reclaim NNN`. Until then the item shows as `working` and nothing is committed, removed or re-dispatched. (3) SKILL.md then allows background workers plus periodic ticks safely, and ends the wait for the slowest worker. Cost: M, about 1–2 days in queue.mjs, tick.mjs, SKILL.md and the model.md Runner section, plus tests beside tick.test.mjs. The 'no liveness threshold' principle holds, because the signal is a file or a pid, not a clock. How we would know it worked: the three experiments in live-worker*.mjs turn into tests that fail today and pass after (a dirty live worktree is untouched and not re-dispatched, a stage-committed branch gets no review, a clean worktree survives), and an external `--watch` run with `runner.spawn` set to a 10-minute sleeping script never produces two workers on one ticket.

SKILL.md:243 prescribes 20–30 min wake-ups, and `--watch` re-ticks every tick.interval (300 s). A headless worker running longer than one interval is therefore reclaimed mid-work and re-dispatched into the same tree. The external runner is broken for any real ticket. title: A conflicting catch-up loops forever: stale, no round, worker stops, reconcile marks it ready, stale again, and the client is never asked
where: Horde land.mjs:3523-3575 (pullParentIntoBranch, then a stale result), tick.mjs:564-575 (stale sends to changes with no round), reference/roles/worker.md:29-34 (a dirty merge means stop and report), queue.mjs:1729-1736 (reconcile marks landed when commits exist, before looking at dirtiness)
evidence: Scratch experiment conflict.mjs: a ticket adds a CHANGELOG entry, a sibling's entry lands on trunk, and the gate returns `stale, no round counted — … conflicts in CHANGELOG.md`. The ticket is re-dispatched. Following the brief, the worker's `git merge mission1/trunk` conflicts (`status AA CHANGELOG.md`) and it stops. The next tick reconciles it straight back to `landed` because a commit exists, and the gate is stale again. Two more cycles printed `cycle 0 [{"a":"changes","round":null}] asks []` and `cycle 1 [{"a":"changes","round":null}] asks []`. The round counter never moves, so the breaker (`stuck`, then an ask) never trips, and every cycle spends a worker spawn. Nothing in any brief tells anyone how to resolve the conflict: land.mjs:2713 says 'Catch the branch up … resolve it there', but worker.md:33 forbids continuing on a dirty merge.
proposal: (a) Stop the loop. Count stale-with-conflict returns separately (`item.staleConflicts`), and on the second one with the same conflicting file set, file a `stop` ask naming the files, or better, route it to the resolver in F3. (b) Give the worker brief a 'catch-up conflict' section, rendered only when the ticket's last land result was stale with conflict files: resolve each file by the rule for its kind (F3), commit the merge, log it. (c) Reconcile checks `git status --porcelain` / MERGE_HEAD before promoting to `landed`, and never marks a tree in mid-merge as ready. Cost: S–M, about 1 day. How we would know it worked: conflict.mjs becomes a test that ends in either a landed ticket or exactly one open ask within 3 ticks, with zero repeated `changes round:null` lines for the same sha.

title: Mechanise the family's known merge conflicts (node logs, locks, append-only files) at catch-up and in the file locks
where: Horde land.mjs:2575-2610 (pullParentIntoBranch aborts on any conflict), land.mjs:364 (DERIVED_LOCK excluded only from scope and batching), tk.mjs:253-254 (only node log.md removed from file locks), queue.mjs:984-997 (lockConflict), queue.mjs:1384-1387 (hubFiles only reported); Yggdrasil docs/the-lock.md:139-182
evidence: Yggdrasil documents a mechanical recipe: "When a committed lock file conflicted as well, the order is: take one side of the lock file, then merge-resolve each conflicted log, then commit, then yg check --approve" (the-lock.md:139), and "Pick one side of the conflicting file wholesale … the lock is self-validating" (:173-180). Horde never calls `yg log merge-resolve` (grep over scripts/: no hits). The 6.1.0 Jarl loop hit these conflicts on almost every merge: "conflict only in CHANGELOG, both entries kept" (translated from Polish; .jarl/log.md:285, 471, 473); "conflicts in CHANGELOG, cli/core/advise/log.md, both locks … locks: our side in full" (translated from Polish; :460); "log conflict … merged as a union, lock taken from release and refilled" (translated from Polish; :1184-1187). It also surfaced four merge-resolve bugs (195, 196, 211, 222; 222 was marked 'urgent, blocks merges' (translated from Polish), :1587). In Horde, a repository where every change adds a CHANGELOG entry either serializes every ticket (the file overlaps in lockConflict) or gets refused by scope if the file is not declared. The plan only lists such 'hub files'.
proposal: Add `config.appendOnly` (a glob list, default the node `log.md` files plus whatever `horde init` detects, e.g. CHANGELOG.md) and a resolver used by pullParentIntoBranch and the batch combine step. (1) For a node `log.md`, run `yg log merge-resolve --node <n>` during the merge. (2) For `yg-lock.*.json`, take the parent's side wholesale; the prose pairs it drops re-judge through F4's path. (3) For an appendOnly file, accept only when diff3 shows both sides as pure additions at the same anchor, then write base, parent's additions, branch's additions. Anything else stays a refusal, as today. Appending entries weakens nothing that protects, so no `lower` ask is involved. Also drop appendOnly files from lockConflict, so they stop serializing the plan. Cost: M, about 2 days, with an e2e test on two tickets touching one node and one CHANGELOG. How we would know it worked: a fixture with 3 parallel tickets on one node, each adding a node log entry and a CHANGELOG line, lands all three with zero stale refusals and zero worker respawns, and the plan's 'hub files' line no longer lists CHANGELOG.md.

title: No way back from a bad landing: no revert tool, the revert is refused once per test file, and `--fate reverted` checks nothing
where: Horde land.mjs:2876-2915 (`--fate reverted` only runs `rev-parse` on the sha), land.mjs:112-121 (the evidence guard refuses a removed test file or a lowered promise), ask.mjs:55-60 (a `lower` ask names exactly one thing), SKILL.md 'the trunk checkout itself is written only by land.mjs'
evidence: Undoing a landed ticket means a revert commit on trunk, which only land.mjs may write, so it has to arrive as a ticket. A ticket whose diff is `git revert -m1 <merge>` removes the test files the bad ticket added, and the evidence guard refuses each one ('a test file removed … refuse — unless the same answered lower ask names … that file'). A ticket that added K test files and flipped P promises to implemented therefore needs K+P separate client asks ('One answered question per thing being lowered, never one for a category'). `--fate reverted --by <sha>` accepts any commit that exists (land.mjs:2897-2900) and does not check that it is on trunk or that it reverts that merge.
proposal: Add a ticket kind `revert` (`tk.mjs new <slug> --reverts NNN`). land.mjs builds the revert commit itself on the ticket branch (`git revert -m1 <landed sha>`) and runs the normal nine items. The three protection guards then measure files the reverted ticket itself introduced against the mission's recorded base-at-start (`archived`/init sha), not against trunk. That keeps SKILL.md's invariant 'no weaker than it found them' literally true, while removing anything that existed before the mission still needs an ask. On merge it records `--fate reverted --by <its own merge sha>` automatically, and `--fate reverted` done by hand checks `git merge-base --is-ancestor <sha> <trunk>` and that the sha's parent tree matches the merge's first parent for the paths it touched. Cost: M, about 2 days. How we would know it worked: a fixture that lands a ticket with 2 tests and a promise, then files a revert ticket, lands it green with zero asks, and the wave close counts 1 reverted; a revert that also deletes a pre-mission test is still refused, naming that file.

v.reason: The mechanics check out: `--fate reverted` only rev-parses the sha, and the evidence guard refuses removed tests without a lower ask for each one. But there is no field evidence that a mission ever needed a revert, and the proposal is M effort with new guard semantics (base-at-start). A reasonable later opportunity, not a 6.1.x priority.

title: Parallelism and seven other defaults are unsourced, and a class-weight 'weight estimate' survived the cost removal
where: Horde scripts/README.md:1640-1664 (constants table), horde.mjs:394-402 (defaults), queue.mjs:1435-1437 and 1565 (weight estimate = class weight × 2), _lib.mjs:688-690 (DEFAULT_CLASSES 1/3/10/30); horde-corrections-loop issues/036 acceptance
evidence: The README's own table says 'Not recorded' for `parallelism` 6, `fixRounds.resume` 3, `fixRounds.fresh` 2, `tick.interval` 300, `territory.maxBytes` 400000, `law.retireAfterWaves` 2, `law.qualityDropAsk` 0.1 and `WAVES_CLEAN_FOR_ENFORCED` 2, against the loop's own rule 'Every constant has a provenance' (translated from Polish; goal.md §4). Issue 036 ruled that `classes` 'stays only if something other than cost uses it' (translated from Polish), yet the plan still prints `weight estimate: … (class weight × 2 runs per ticket)`, a cost proxy with invented weights. The real limits seen in the field were gate time (issue 052: about 10 min per gate, 20 branches queued, about 3 h to drain) and the account's rate limits (2026-09-09 review, A17), not a fixed count of 6.
proposal: (1) Drop the weight estimate from `plan`, or rename it and give the weights a source. Keep `classes` only as the model-class ladder (classUp). (3) Ask Krzysztof to source or accept each 'Not recorded' row, one by one. Cost: S, about half a day plus one ruling. How we would know it worked: the constants table has no 'Not recorded' rows without a dated ruling, and `grep -n 'weight estimate' queue.mjs` returns nothing, or returns a sourced line.
